text:
marie-support: FYI customer Acme Data escalated — their AWS Marketplace invoice line item for 'AI Inference - token usage' shows 1,234,567 tokens billed but our usage dashboard shows 1,052,300 for the same billing window. They're asking for a reconciliation and are pretty worried about the delta. Any quick theories? :eyes:

javier-billing: Can you paste the invoice ID + the exact marketplace line item text/sku? AWS sometimes aggregates across regions or reports in different unit granularity. Also did they have any reserved capacity/commit on their account?

marie-support: Invoice ID: INV-2109-ACME, AWS UsageRecordId: aws-mlk-987654, Marketplace SKU: redwood-inf-usage. Quoted line on invoice: "AI Inference - token usage" Qty: 1,234,567 units (tokens) period: 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28. Our dashboard query for acct_acme for that period returns 1,052,300 tokens. Customer says they didn't change workload except a load test on 2026-02-14. I'm attaching their screenshots in the case.

aws-billing-bot: Marketplace metering event: Reservation BRK-20260312-01234 recorded -> count=1234567, recorded_at=2026-03-12T07:32:10Z (automated).

sam-ops: A few likely causes off the top: 1) AWS Marketplace reports aggregated/bucketed counts (e.g., rounds up hourly or per-minute metering). 2) We might be attributing tokens to a different customer id if they used multiple API keys or a proxy. 3) Reserved/commit adjustments or credits applied on invoice level. 4) Edge-case double-count from a replayer job or retry storms.

sam-ops: Quick repro steps I recommend: 
- Run our internal usage exporter for acct_acme for 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28 with hourly granularity: 
```
python tools/usage_report.py --customer acct_acme --start 2026-02-01 --end 2026-02-28 --granularity hourly > /tmp/acme_hourly.csv
```
- Cross-check with metering events in S3 (s3://marketplace-metering/2026/02/) for that account id and match timestamps.
- Check for API key rotation: `SELECT api_key, count(*) FROM token_usage WHERE customer='acct_acme' AND ts BETWEEN ... GROUP BY api_key;`

ellie-cs: Customer confirmed they used the same API key except during the 02/14 test — but they said the test was short and shouldn't account for ~180k tokens difference. They're asking for an ETA to provide them an answer.

akshay-engr: I can run a ledger re-aggregation for acct_acme for Feb window (non-destructive, write to a report bucket) and output per-request token attribution. Need billing ops sign-off to pull marketplace metering logs and crosswalk. Estimated run time ~20min. If there are multiple model aliases we should map them to the same billing SKU first.

javier-billing: Please go ahead akshay. Also I'll open a Billing Support case with AWS to request the marketplace "usage record detail" for that invoice period (AWS sometimes shows line-item-level bucketing or offer-level rounding). Also check whether any committed usage discounts were applied that modify invoice-level totals.

marie-support: Approved — akshay please run it and paste the report link here. I'll tell the customer ETA ~4 hours and that we're digging into line-item granularity and possible aggregation differences. Thanks all. :mag_right:

akshay-engr: Kicking off re-agg job now. Command run: `./bin/reaggregate_ledger --customer acct_acme --start 2026-02-01 --end 2026-02-28 --output s3://redwood-recon/acme/2026-02/recon.csv` I'll post results when finished.

aws-billing-bot: Note: AWS meter record BRK-20260312-01234 has dimension=redwood-inf-usage; detail-level=hourly (per AWS metering service).

javier-billing: After akshay's report we should: 1) compare per-hour counts (our calc vs AWS metering), 2) verify if any invoice-level adjustments/credits were applied, 3) prepare a short explainer for the customer describing any rounding/aggregation mismatch and next steps if we find a bug.

marie-support: I'll draft the customer message once we have the report. Thanks team.

akshay-engr: Report uploaded: s3://redwood-recon/acme/2026-02/recon.csv -> preliminary totals: our_recount=1,052,298 tokens, metering_events_sum=1,234,567 tokens. There's a cluster of metering events on 2026-02-14 02:00-03:00 UTC showing large counts — investigating whether those are replayed batched writes from a partner integration.

marie-support: Copying customer on progress. If anyone finds it's an AWS aggregation/rounding issue, we'll ask them to request the usage detail through their AWS console as well.

ellie-cs: Customer replied: thanks, please escalate if you see anything suspicious — their finance team is ready to review a reconciliation spreadsheet.

javier-billing: I'll hold until AWS returns usage detail. If we confirm it's on our side (double-count bug or attribution), we'll issue a credit and note root cause.

marie-support: Closing loop for now — will update thread when AWS responds or when akshay confirms root cause.
